method: Three read-only sub-agent audits of current code; original Mouse Thumb scan/document and BUGS.md were not supplied or reproduced.

tests.note: Targeted expression, loft/thicken real-kernel, B-spline and kernel-guard tests.

items.detail: Parametric expression-driven thicken/open faces, validity checks and self-intersection query exist; historical scan-specific crashes need current-build reproduction.
Associative loft and continuity exist; guide/boundary inputs missing.
Native exception guards exist; result validation, diagnostics, variable radius and setbacks remain.
Internal stable edge references exist; persistent MCP reference API and rule selectors missing.
Raw sweep/projection exist; associative surface-curve features missing.
Construction and run_program expression support exist.
Feature cache invalidates for unrelated variables; live asynchronous progress missing.
Periodic/closed, chord/centripetal/uniform, single-edge and raw control-point NURBS exist; parametric control-point sketches missing.
Explicit curved-face toObject and throughAll exist; from-face and automatic next/body extents missing.
Exception guards, crash detection, between-op cancellation and full BRepCheck shape.checkShape exist; worker, in-flight cancellation and recovery missing.
Subshape lists can return references evicted during the same call.
MeshNode display/opacity exist; mesh-only scan import and deviation measurement missing.
STL tolerance, bytes/resources and separate-file batch export missing.
Appending an extrude ignores the supplied feature name.

tasks.title: Reject invalid fillet and chamfer results
tasks.gap: Tracked and untracked fillet/chamfer paths accept IsDone() without a BRepCheck_Analyzer validity check. The user reported an invalid perimeter fillet on free-form geometry; that scan-specific result has not been reproduced on this build.
tasks.acceptance: Validate tracked and untracked results before accepting them; return Result errors for invalid shapes. Add a free-form regression showing later booleans remain safe.

tasks.title: Report actionable fillet and chamfer failure diagnostics
tasks.gap: Failures currently return generic Failed to fillet / Failed to chamfer messages. Native exception guards exist, but users cannot distinguish impossible geometry from an excessive radius or tangency problem.
tasks.acceptance: Surface available OCCT diagnostics; identify radius and tangent-face failures when determinable, without claiming unsupported certainty.

tasks.title: Support variable-radius fillets
tasks.gap: Fillets expose one radius ParameterValue; the kernel adds a constant radius per edge. The reported free-form model needs radius variation.
tasks.acceptance: Provide an editable radius law along selected edges, expression evaluation and stable reference handling; validate the resulting B-rep.

tasks.title: Support fillet corner setbacks
tasks.gap: The public feature and kernel wrapper expose no corner-setback controls. The user requested setbacks at difficult free-form edge junctions.
tasks.acceptance: Expose corner setbacks independently of constant-radius selection, with validation and useful failures.

tasks.title: Support guide and boundary curves in parametric lofts
tasks.gap: Associative loft, ruled/solid options and continuity are already implemented. LoftOp has no guide or boundary curve references.
tasks.acceptance: Add associative guide/boundary inputs that follow upstream edits, preserve existing continuity options and reject incompatible curve/section combinations clearly.

tasks.title: Expose persistent edge references through MCP
tasks.gap: Internal edge references already capture tracked IDs/fingerprints and re-resolve after rebuild. MCP callers still supply edgeIndexes and cannot query/reuse persistent references across calls.
tasks.acceptance: Expose existing persistent identifiers for query and fillet/chamfer selection; prove a reference survives an upstream change that reorders edges.

tasks.title: Add rule-based edge selection through MCP
tasks.gap: Callers must manually pick raw indexes even though the application tracks topology internally. Python BREP traversal was needed to identify edges in the reported model.
tasks.acceptance: Select edges by feature origin, adjoining face sets, outline/curve membership and analytic geometry such as cylinder radius/elevation; return stable references and explain empty/ambiguous matches.

tasks.title: Add a parametric sweep along a 3D path
tasks.gap: Low-level run_program sweep exists; the parametric operation catalog contains no sweep. Profile/path edits therefore cannot drive an associative sweep.
tasks.acceptance: Add editable profile and 3D-path references, rebuild dependencies and tracked output topology, reusing the existing low-level sweep.

tasks.title: Add associative curve projection onto surfaces
tasks.gap: Low-level directional curveProjection already exists, but projection is absent from the parametric feature catalog.
tasks.acceptance: Add associative curve/target-face references and projection direction; edits to either input update the projected result.

tasks.title: Add a parametric groove or rib along a curve on a face
tasks.gap: No associative face-curve groove/rib operation exists. The reported model could not express the design crease, pad outline or rim lip.
tasks.acceptance: Add an editable profile/curve/face feature with cut or join behavior, usable on curved walls; rebuild when its referenced geometry changes.

tasks.title: Invalidate feature caches only for dependent variables
tasks.gap: Per-feature caching exists, but each cache key serializes the entire variable scope. An unrelated variable edit invalidates otherwise reusable feature results.
tasks.acceptance: Track variable dependencies including transitive expressions; an unrelated edit causes zero geometry evaluations, while affected features and downstream consumers rebuild.

tasks.title: Expose asynchronous rebuild progress through MCP
tasks.gap: Long rebuilds block the main thread and can exceed the relay's 120-second timeout. Between-operation checks and post-call warnings provide no live progress.
tasks.acceptance: Offer asynchronous rebuild status/progress and a completion result for long operations; keep status observable while work is running. Coordinate with worker execution.

tasks.title: Support control-point and weighted NURBS in parametric sketches
tasks.gap: Periodic, chord/centripetal/uniform fit-point B-splines and single-edge output already exist; low-level run_program control-point NURBS exists too. Parametric sketch authoring still accepts interpolating fit points only.
tasks.acceptance: Expose editable control poles/weights and knot/degree settings for parametric sketch entities, while preserving existing fit-point behavior.

tasks.title: Add an associative from-face extrusion start
tasks.gap: Extrusion offers startOffset but no start-face reference. Explicit up-to-object and through-all end extents already exist. Bosses/ribs on curved walls still need a hand-computed start offset.
tasks.acceptance: Start an extrusion from a selected target face, including curved walls; track that face and update the start after upstream edits. Related existing extent work: #59 and #60.

tasks.title: Add automatic up-to-next-face or body extrusion extent
tasks.gap: Distance, through-all and explicit to-object face extents exist, but automatic up-to-next/body selection does not.
tasks.acceptance: Find the next valid target intersection along the extrusion direction for bosses/ribs on curved walls; avoid manual face selection and report absent/ambiguous targets. Related: #59 and #60.

tasks.title: Run expensive kernel operations in a bounded worker
tasks.gap: The OCCT kernel runs synchronously on the main thread, blocking tools/UI. KERNEL-01 already describes a bounded worker design, but it is not implemented. Existing #50/#51 discuss open-time blocking and performance; this task is specifically kernel execution.
tasks.acceptance: Implement the existing worker design with explicit time bounds; keep document/status queries and UI responsive during long geometry calls. Preserve serialized tool ordering and reference semantics.

tasks.title: Cancel an in-flight kernel operation
tasks.gap: Cancellation checks occur only between synchronous operations. An individual hung/slow OCCT call cannot be interrupted. KERNEL-01 describes worker timeout/cancellation.
tasks.acceptance: Cancel an active geometry call promptly, recover the execution context, and leave the document unchanged or rolled back. Coordinate with worker execution; distinguish cancellation from failure.

tasks.title: Recover a crashed kernel without reloading the tab
tasks.gap: Native exception guards and crash detection already exist. A confirmed fatal kernel crash remains final for the page; current guidance requires reload. Existing OccShape handles belong to the old module, so merely calling initWasm again is insufficient.
tasks.acceptance: Recreate the kernel execution context and rebuild valid document geometry safely, retaining edits and stable feature references; reject reuse of handles from the old module. Follow KERNEL-01.

tasks.title: Add compact run_parametric responses
tasks.gap: Every touched body returns the entire summarized feature list; MCP schema has no summary/quiet option. User reports 25–60 kB replies for simple edits.
tasks.acceptance: Add an explicit compact response mode returning created/changed features and essential errors/status only, while keeping the existing full response available.

tasks.title: Do not return subshape references already evicted from the ref store
tasks.gap: The store cap is 256. registerRef evicts old entries while findSubShapes registers a whole list, then returns every generated reference. A 600-edge response can therefore contain 344 already unusable references.
tasks.acceptance: Ensure every returned reference is usable immediately; support large results with a larger/bounded store, pagination or index queries. Add a >256-subshape regression and document lifetime semantics.

tasks.title: Import scan files as lightweight reference MeshNodes
tasks.gap: MeshNode rendering and opacity already exist. Default STL import instead converts the scan through OCCT into a B-rep; no production mesh-only scan import path was found.
tasks.acceptance: Add an explicit reference-mesh import path that reuses existing MeshNode storage/rendering and ghost opacity, with placement/visibility controls and no geometry-kernel conversion.

tasks.title: Measure CAD-to-reference-mesh deviation
tasks.gap: Reference mesh infrastructure exists, but production code has no CAD-to-scan deviation measurement. The user needs model-quality comparisons inside CAD.
tasks.acceptance: Measure deviation against a reference mesh and present useful values/visualization, with documented units, sampling and accuracy. Coordinate with reference-mesh import.

tasks.title: Expose STL tessellation tolerance in export
tasks.gap: StlExportOptions currently exposes binary/name, with no caller-selected tessellation tolerance.
tasks.acceptance: Expose validated tessellation tolerances through STL export and MCP; demonstrate that tolerance changes fidelity/file size without changing CAD geometry.

tasks.title: Return exported model bytes or a resource through MCP
tasks.gap: MCP export unconditionally triggers a browser download. Agents cannot receive the exported data or an accessible resource directly.
tasks.acceptance: Offer an export result containing bytes or a retrievable resource, with filename/MIME metadata and payload limits; keep browser download available. A local filesystem path must have defined supported semantics.

tasks.title: Batch-export separate model files without repeated downloads
tasks.gap: Exporting multiple ids currently merges them into one file. There is no separate-output/archive batch mode, and separate browser downloads can trigger a multiple-download prompt.
tasks.acceptance: Export requested models as distinct files in one archive or batch resource response, preserving filenames and reporting per-output errors.

tasks.title: Honor extrude names when appending to an existing body
tasks.gap: For extrude with body/operation, ExtrudeFeatureData is created without op.name. The supplied name is only used when creating a new body, so every appended feature needs a separate rename.
tasks.acceptance: Apply the caller's name to the appended extrusion feature for join/cut; test both operations and ensure the target body's existing name remains correct.

saveFormat: Frozen: any persisted-schema change requires explicit prior boss approval; this audit makes no implementation changes.
